beats.say: Messengers are handy. But a work file sent to a personal account leaves your organisation's control, sometimes for years.
A familiar name on a new number may really be a scammer. Check by calling the old number you already know.

body.text: Hello, Narmina. It is Elchin Gasimov.
This is my new number, I lost the old one.
The director urgently needs a report.
Send the finance spreadsheet right here.
I am in a meeting, I cannot talk, just text.

beats.say: Disappearing messages help, but the other person can still take a screenshot. Keep sensitive information out of messengers altogether.
For work, use the tool your organisation approved. Not sure which one? Ask your technical support team.

scenes.prompt: What is suspicious in this chat?

body.text: Hello, Narmina. It is Elchin Gasimov.
This is my new number, I lost the old one.
The director urgently needs a report.
Send the finance spreadsheet right here.
I am in a meeting, I cannot talk, just text.

spots.label: Unsaved number
spots.explain: No name, only a number. The only proof of who it is comes from the sender.

spots.label: The new number story
spots.explain: This is the most common opener. Call the old number to check.

spots.label: Work file into a messenger
spots.explain: Finance documents go only through an approved work channel.

spots.label: Avoids a call
spots.explain: A scammer does not want you to hear the voice. Be wary of any request that refuses a call.

question.prompt: How do you check it is really Elchin?

options.label: I call the new number
options.feedback: That number belongs to the scammer. They can answer themselves or with a faked voice.

options.label: I call his old number or office line
options.feedback: Correct. A channel you already know is the most reliable check.

options.label: I look at the profile photo
options.feedback: Copying a photo from the internet takes a minute.

options.label: I ask him for the office address
options.feedback: That is public information. Anyone can answer it.

scenes.explain: Always verify through a channel you already know: the old number, the office line, or in person.

scenes.prompt: Is this message safe or risky?

cards.explain: A work file landed in the family group. Mistakes like this happen most when we rush.

body.text: Remote access password: Baki2026! Everyone use it.

cards.explain: A shared password posted in a large group. Lose one phone and access opens for everyone.

body.text: I uploaded the final report to the internal system, please look there.

cards.explain: The file itself is not sent, it stays in the internal system. That is the right way.
Nothing sensitive, just a reminder. Keep documents and figures in the approved channel.

body.text: To check your salary, send photos of both sides of your ID card.

cards.explain: The accounts office already has your details. An ID photo is used to open fake accounts.

nodes.text: You accidentally sent the staff phone list to a neighbourhood group of 300 people. Two minutes have passed.

choices.label: I delete it for everyone and tell my manager now
choices.feedback: A good start. Deleting slows the spread, reporting limits the damage.

choices.label: I quietly delete it, surely no one saw
choices.feedback: Someone may already have downloaded it. If you stay silent, no one can act in time.

choices.label: I do nothing, it is too late anyway
choices.feedback: The file stays in the group and spreads. It is not too late, act now.

nodes.text: What exactly was in the file?
nodes.speaker: Manager
nodes.spoken: <breath> What exactly was in the file?

choices.label: I say exactly: names and mobile numbers of 120 staff
choices.feedback: An honest, precise answer speeds up the response.

choices.label: I play it down: just an unimportant table
choices.feedback: A team that does not know what leaked cannot decide well. Your colleagues will not be ready for scam calls.

nodes.text: Someone in the group writes: I opened the file, interesting. What do you do?

choices.label: I politely ask him to delete it and tell my manager
choices.feedback: Well done. You tried to stop the spread and reported everything openly.

choices.label: I argue with him and make threats
choices.feedback: Threats raise tension and make the file more interesting. Ask politely and let the organisation handle the rest.

points: Send work files only through the approved tool.
Check a new number through a channel you already know.
If you send to the wrong place, delete and report at once.
